data: This course provides a foundational understanding of stereochemistry, the study of the three-dimensional arrangement of atoms in molecules and its impact on chemical behavior. Topics include chirality, enantiomers, diastereomers, conformational analysis, stereoisomerism in organic and inorganic systems, and the influence of symmetry elements. The course emphasizes the role of stereochemistry in physical and chemical properties, reactivity, and biological activity, with examples from natural products, pharmaceuticals, and materials. Students will develop skills in visualizing and representing stereochemical relationships, and in applying stereochemical principles to predict molecular interactions and reaction outcomes.
